newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Nobel winner says medical research must be kept up.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Nobel winner says medical research must be kept up.

text.p: Australian Nobel Medicine Prize winner Peter Doherty said on Tuesday he would use his new-found prestige to fight against funding cuts for medical research.
Doherty said the US$1.12 million award carried an obligation to champion biomedical research.
"It ... carries certain responsibilities with it, I think, to speak for science, to speak for biomedical research," he said in a radio interview."
Doherty, 55, and Swiss Rolf Zinkernagel, 52, received the prestigious award for joint research in Australia between 1973 and 1975.
The two men discovered how the immune system recognises and can then kill virus-infected cells, unlocking the mystery of how a vaccine needs to be composed.

"We are at the most important phase of biomedical research in my career, I mean enormously important things are happening and happening very quickly due to advances in technology," said Doherty, who now works at a cancer hospital in Memphis, in the United States.

"At the same time, every western government is looking to cut expenses and (is) worried about their tax base and so forth, and I think it's very easy to sacrifice things like research because there's not such a well-organised constituency to fight for it.
"But it's enormously important that we keep it going because this is the centre of a lot of our science and a lot of our technological development."

Doherty, who has lived in the United States for several years, said he could not comment on the funding situation in Australia, where funds have been slashed by the new conservative government as part of a budget deficit reduction programme.
